title: Magnetic materials, domains and permeability; Fields of currents (quantitative); Force on moving charges
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: NEW-magnetic-materials-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; NEW-magnetic-materials-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; NEW-magnetic-materials-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; NEW-magnetic-materials-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG03-1#N.3a, MG04-1#N.3, NEW-magnetic-materials-1#N.2, MG03-1#N.6b, MG04-1#N.5, NEW-magnetic-materials-1#N.5, MG03-1#N.12b, MG04-1#N.12b, NEW-magnetic-materials-1#N.11, MG03-1#N.17, MG04-1#N.13, MG04-1#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Domain
items.clue: Small region of iron in which the atomic dipoles line up with those next to them.

items.label: Permeability
items.clue: Symbol μ: how strongly the dipoles of a substance align in response to an external field.

items.label: Ferromagnetic
items.clue: Describes iron, nickel and cobalt: strongly attracted, and able to stay aligned permanently.

items.label: Diamagnetic
items.clue: Describes the weak response, opposite to the field, that dominates in copper, water and bismuth.

questions.stem: An electron moves toward the right side of the page through a uniform magnetic field directed out of the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force exerted on the electron at this instant?

options.text: Toward the top of the page
Toward the bottom of the page
Out of the page, along B
Left, opposite its motion

questions.stem: A long straight wire of diameter 0.010 m carries a current of 12 A. Point P is 0.045 m from the surface of the wire. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field produced by the wire at P? (Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.)
Which of the following produces a magnetic field? Ignore Earth's field and Earth's motion.

options.text: A charged plastic ring held at rest on a stand
A charged plastic ring spinning about its central axis
An uncharged copper ring spinning about its central axis
An unmagnetized iron ring, held at rest on a stand

questions.stem: A proton moves in a circular path of radius r in a uniform magnetic field, with its velocity perpendicular to the field. A second proton moves in the same field with twice the speed, its velocity also perpendicular to the field. Only magnetic forces are exerted on the protons. The radius of the second proton's circular path is kr. What is k?

options.text: ½

questions.stem: Two long straight parallel wires, 1 and 2, are a distance d apart. Wire 1 carries a current I, and wire 2 carries a current 3I in the same direction. Point P is on the line joining the wires, between them, at the location where the net magnetic field produced by the two wires is zero. Ignore Earth's magnetic field. Which expression gives the distance from wire 1 to P?

An iron nail does not attract a steel paper clip. After the nail has been stroked several times in one direction with one pole of a strong magnet, it does attract the paper clip. Which explanation of these observations is correct?

options.text: It contained no magnetic dipoles until the stroking created them
The stroking moved some of the magnet's magnetism into the nail
The stroking charged its ends oppositely, as rubbing charges a balloon
Its domains pointed in random directions until stroking aligned them

questions.stem: A proton moves at 2.0 × 10⁴ m/s toward the right side of the page through a region that contains a uniform electric field of magnitude 3.0 × 10³ N/C directed toward the bottom of the page and a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.050 T directed into the page. The gravitational force on the proton is negligible. What is the magnitude of the net force exerted on the proton at this instant? (Use e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.)

Two long straight parallel wires are 0.040 m apart. Wire 1 carries a current of 12 A, and wire 2 carries a current of 8.0 A in the opposite direction. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force exerted by wire 1 on a 1.5 m length of wire 2? (Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.)

Rods of nickel, aluminum and copper, identical in size and shape, are each placed in turn in a strong external magnetic field and then removed from it. Which of the rods can then be a permanent magnet?

options.text: The nickel and aluminum rods, which were both attracted
All three rods, since all three of them are metals
None of them, as their dipoles return to random directions
The nickel rod alone, as its domains can stay aligned

questions.stem: Two protons enter two separate regions at the same speed. Region 1 contains only a uniform electric field; region 2 contains only a uniform magnetic field. Each proton enters at right angles to the field lines. Gravity is negligible. A short time later, which statement is correct?

options.text: Both protons still have their starting speed, because each force began at right angles to the motion.
Only the proton in the magnetic field still has its starting speed.
Only the proton in the electric field still has its starting speed.
Both protons have sped up, because each one is pushed by a force.

questions.stem: Two long straight parallel wires, X and Y, are 5.0 cm apart in air. X carries 2.0 A and Y carries 6.0 A, in the same direction. What is the magnetic force on a 1.0 m length of each wire?

options.text: 4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N on X; 1.4 × 10⁻⁴ N on Y
4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N on each, towards the other wire
1.6 × 10⁻⁵ N on X; 4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N on Y
4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N on each, away from the other wire

questions.explanation: Field of X at Y: 2 × 10⁻⁷ × 2.0 ÷ 0.050 = 8.0 × 10⁻⁶ T. Force on 1.0 m of Y: 8.0 × 10⁻⁶ × 6.0 × 1.0 = 4.8 × 10⁻⁵ N. Newton's third law: the force on X is the same size, and same-direction currents attract.

questions.stem: A light, loosely wound coil of wire, like a soft spring, hangs vertically. A large steady current is passed through it. What happens to the length of the coil?

options.text: It gets shorter: neighbouring turns carry current the same way, so they attract.
It gets longer, because neighbouring turns carry like currents, and like currents repel.
It stays the same, because the coil's own field cannot exert a force on the coil itself.
It gets longer, because the field inside the coil pushes the turns apart along its axis.

questions.explanation: Each turn is like a parallel wire beside the next, with current the same way: they pull together and the coil contracts.
